paragraphs.text: At that season Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,
paragraphs.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἤκουσεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὴν ἀκοὴν Ἰησοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: En ekeinō tō kairō ēkousen Hērōdēs ho tetraarchēs tēn akoēn Iēsou,

paragraphs.text: and said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead; and therefore do these powers work in him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστής· αὐτὸς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen tois paisin autou· Houtos estin Iōannēs ho baptistēs· autos ēgerthē apo tōn nekrōn, kai dia touto hai dynameis energousin en autō.

paragraphs.text: For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip`s wife.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης κρατήσας τὸν Ἰωάννην ἔδησεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ ἀπέθετο διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Ho gar Hērōdēs kratēsas ton Iōannēn edēsen auton kai en phylakē apetheto dia Hērōdiada tēn gynaika Philippou tou adelphou autou,

paragraphs.text: For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν αὐτήν·
paragraphs.translit: elegen gar autō ho Iōannēs· Ouk exestin soi echein autēn·

paragraphs.text: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
paragraphs.original: καὶ θέλων αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἐφοβήθη τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ὡς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.
paragraphs.translit: kai thelōn auton apokteinai ephobēthē ton ochlon, hoti hōs prophētēn auton eichon.

paragraphs.text: But when Herod`s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst, and pleased Herod.
paragraphs.original: γενεσίοις δὲ γενομένοις τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ὠρχήσατο ἡ θυγάτηρ τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καὶ ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ,
paragraphs.translit: genesiois de genomenois tou Hērōdou ōrchēsato hē thygatēr tēs Hērōdiados en tō mesō kai ēresen tō Hērōdē,

paragraphs.text: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she should ask.
paragraphs.original: ὅθεν μετὰ ὅρκου ὡμολόγησεν αὐτῇ δοῦναι ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσηται.
paragraphs.translit: hothen meta horkou hōmologēsen autē dounai ho ean aitēsētai.

paragraphs.text: And she, being put forward by her mother, saith, Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ προβιβασθεῖσα ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς· Δός μοι, φησίν, ὧδε ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hē de probibastheisa hypo tēs mētros autēs· Dos moi, phēsin, hōde epi pinaki tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou baptistou.

paragraphs.text: And the king was grieved; but for the sake of his oaths, and of them that sat at meat with him, he commanded it to be given;
paragraphs.original: καὶ λυπηθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς συνανακειμένους ἐκέλευσεν δοθῆναι,
paragraphs.translit: kai lypētheis ho basileus dia tous horkous kai tous synanakeimenous ekeleusen dothēnai,

paragraphs.text: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πέμψας ἀπεκεφάλισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ·
paragraphs.translit: kai pempsas apekephalisen ton Iōannēn en tē phylakē·

paragraphs.text: And his head was brought on a platter, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠνέχθη ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἐδόθη τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ ἤνεγκεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēnechthē hē kephalē autou epi pinaki kai edothē tō korasiō, kai ēnenken tē mētri autēs.

paragraphs.text: And his disciples came, and took up the corpse, and buried him; and they went and told Jesus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai proselthontes hoi mathētai autou ēran to ptōma kai ethapsan auton, kai elthontes apēngeilan tō Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: Now when Jesus heard [it], he withdrew from thence in a boat, to a desert place apart: and when the multitudes heard [thereof,] they followed him on foot from the cities.
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν ἐν πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατʼ ἰδίαν· καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πεζῇ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλεων.
paragraphs.translit: Akousas de ho Iēsous anechōrēsen ekeithen en ploiō eis erēmon topon katʼ idian· kai akousantes hoi ochloi ēkolouthēsan autō pezē apo tōn poleōn.

paragraphs.text: And he came forth, and saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, and healed their sick.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν τοὺς ἀρρώστους αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthōn eiden polyn ochlon, kai esplanchnisthē epʼ autois kai etherapeusen tous arrōstous autōn.

paragraphs.text: And when even was come, the disciples came to him, saying, The place is desert, and the time is already past; send the multitudes away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves food.
paragraphs.original: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἡ ὥρα ἤδη παρῆλθεν· ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ὄχλους, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὰς κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς βρώματα.
paragraphs.translit: opsias de genomenēs prosēlthon autō hoi mathētai legontes· Erēmos estin ho topos kai hē hōra ēdē parēlthen· apolyson tous ochlous, hina apelthontes eis tas kōmas agorasōsin heautois brōmata.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus said unto them, They have no need to go away; give ye them to eat.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν ἀπελθεῖν· δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Ou chreian echousin apelthein· dote autois hymeis phagein.

paragraphs.text: And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οὐκ ἔχομεν ὧδε εἰ μὴ πέντε ἄρτους καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de legousin autō· Ouk echomen hōde ei mē pente artous kai dyo ichthyas.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Bring them hither to me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Φέρετέ μοι ὧδε αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Pherete moi hōde autous.

paragraphs.text: And he commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass; and he took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κελεύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνακλιθῆναι ἐπὶ τοῦ χόρτου, λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας, ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἔδωκεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.
paragraphs.translit: kai keleusas tous ochlous anaklithēnai epi tou chortou, labōn tous pente artous kai tous dyo ichthyas, anablepsas eis ton ouranon eulogēsen kai klasas edōken tois mathētais tous artous hoi de mathētai tois ochlois.

paragraphs.text: And they all ate, and were filled: and they took up that which remained over of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις.
paragraphs.translit: kai ephagon pantes kai echortasthēsan, kai ēran to perisseuon tōn klasmatōn dōdeka kophinous plēreis.

paragraphs.text: And they that did eat were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ πεντακισχίλιοι χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de esthiontes ēsan andres hōsei pentakischilioi chōris gynaikōn kai paidiōn.

paragraphs.text: And straightway he constrained the disciples to enter into the boat, and to go before him unto the other side, till he should send the multitudes away.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εὐθέως ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι εἰς πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πέραν, ἕως οὗ ἀπολύσῃ τοὺς ὄχλους.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eutheōs ēnankasen tous mathētas embēnai eis ploion kai proagein auton eis to peran, heōs hou apolysē tous ochlous.

paragraphs.text: And after he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into the mountain apart to pray: and when even was come, he was there alone.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατʼ ἰδίαν προσεύξασθαι. ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης μόνος ἦν ἐκεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai apolysas tous ochlous anebē eis to oros katʼ idian proseuxasthai. opsias de genomenēs monos ēn ekei.

paragraphs.text: But the boat was now in the midst of the sea, distressed by the waves; for the wind was contrary.
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ πλοῖον ἤδη σταδίους πολλοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀπεῖχεν, βασανιζόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, ἦν γὰρ ἐναντίος ὁ ἄνεμος.
paragraphs.translit: to de ploion ēdē stadious pollous apo tēs gēs apeichen, basanizomenon hypo tōn kymatōn, ēn gar enantios ho anemos.

paragraphs.text: And in the fourth watch of the night he came unto them, walking upon the sea.
paragraphs.original: τετάρτῃ δὲ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτὸς ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν.
paragraphs.translit: tetartē de phylakē tēs nyktos ēlthen pros autous peripatōn epi tēn thalassan.

paragraphs.text: And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a ghost; and they cried out for fear.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἐταράχθησαν λέγοντες ὅτι Φάντασμά ἐστιν, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου ἔκραξαν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de mathētai idontes auton epi tēs thalassēs peripatounta etarachthēsan legontes hoti Phantasma estin, kai apo tou phobou ekraxan.

paragraphs.text: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
paragraphs.original: εὐθὺς δὲ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι· μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
paragraphs.translit: euthys de elalēsen autois ho Iēsous legōn· Tharseite, egō eimi· mē phobeisthe.

paragraphs.text: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto the upon the waters.
paragraphs.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Κύριε, εἰ σὺ εἶ, κέλευσόν με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα·
paragraphs.translit: Apokritheis de autō ho Petros eipen· Kyrie, ei sy ei, keleuson me elthein pros se epi ta hydata·

paragraphs.text: And he said, Come. And Peter went down from the boat, and walked upon the waters to come to Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐλθέ. καὶ καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου Πέτρος περιεπάτησεν ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα καὶ ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Elthe. kai katabas apo tou ploiou Petros periepatēsen epi ta hydata kai ēlthen pros ton Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: But when he saw the wind, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, Lord, save me.
paragraphs.original: βλέπων δὲ τὸν ἄνεμον ἰσχυρὸν ἐφοβήθη, καὶ ἀρξάμενος καταποντίζεσθαι ἔκραξεν λέγων· Κύριε, σῶσόν με.
paragraphs.translit: blepōn de ton anemon ischyron ephobēthē, kai arxamenos katapontizesthai ekraxen legōn· Kyrie, sōson me.

paragraphs.text: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and took hold of him, and saith unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
paragraphs.original: εὐθέως δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὀλιγόπιστε, εἰς τί ἐδίστασας;
paragraphs.translit: eutheōs de ho Iēsous ekteinas tēn cheira epelabeto autou kai legei autō· Oligopiste, eis ti edistasas;

paragraphs.text: And when they were gone up into the boat, the wind ceased.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναβάντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος.
paragraphs.translit: kai anabantōn autōn eis to ploion ekopasen ho anemos.

paragraphs.text: And they that were in the boat worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς εἶ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de en tō ploiō prosekynēsan autō legontes· Alēthōs theou hyios ei.

paragraphs.text: And when they had crossed over, they came to the land, unto Gennesaret.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς Γεννησαρέτ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai diaperasantes ēlthon epi tēn gēn eis Gennēsaret.

paragraphs.text: And when the men of that place knew him, they sent into all that region round about, and brought unto him all that were sick,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ἀπέστειλαν εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον ἐκείνην, καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας,
paragraphs.translit: kai epignontes auton hoi andres tou topou ekeinou apesteilan eis holēn tēn perichōron ekeinēn, kai prosēnenkan autō pantas tous kakōs echontas,

paragraphs.text: and they besought him that they might only touch the border of his garment: and as many as touched were made whole.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μόνον ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ· καὶ ὅσοι ἥψαντο διεσώθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai parekaloun auton hina monon hapsōntai tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou· kai hosoi hēpsanto diesōthēsan.
